field_note.yearofice.title: Field note
field_note.yearofice.needle_tea.fact: Spruce tips carry vitamin C, and boiled needle tea kept northern travellers free of scurvy.
field_note.yearofice.needle_tea.rule: Eat or brew them to hold off the slow weakness of a diet with no fresh plants.
field_note.yearofice.rose_hips.fact: Rose hips hold more vitamin C than most fruit by weight and stay on the bush through winter.
field_note.yearofice.rose_hips.rule: They are a winter vitamin source here: pick them late, when little else is left.
field_note.yearofice.blueberries.fact: Wild blueberries ripen in late summer and are mostly water and sugar, with little fat or protein.
field_note.yearofice.blueberries.rule: Berries fill the stomach and give quick energy, but they will not carry you through a week.
field_note.yearofice.lingonberries.fact: Lingonberries keep through winter in the cold because their natural benzoic acid slows spoilage.
field_note.yearofice.lingonberries.rule: Frozen lingonberries stay good far longer than soft berries.
field_note.yearofice.cranberries.fact: Cranberries are tart and acidic, and keep for months in the cold.
field_note.yearofice.cranberries.rule: They store well, so a cache of them is worth the walk.
field_note.yearofice.birch_bark.fact: Birch bark burns even when wet, because it is rich in oils.
field_note.yearofice.birch_bark.rule: Birch bark is your best tinder starter in rain or snow.
field_note.yearofice.tinder_bundle.fact: A tinder bundle is shaped like a bird's nest so air reaches the ember from every side.
field_note.yearofice.tinder_bundle.rule: Blow gently: too hard and the ember dies, too soft and it will not catch.
field_note.yearofice.cordage.fact: Twisting plant fibre in two plies that wind against each other makes a rope that will not unravel.
field_note.yearofice.cordage.rule: Cordage binds the bow drill, the snare and the pack frame.
field_note.yearofice.sinew.fact: Sinew from the back of a large animal dries hard and, wet, becomes a strong glue-backed thread.
field_note.yearofice.sinew.rule: Sinew is cordage you can only get from a kill.
field_note.yearofice.raw_hide.fact: A raw hide rots in days if left untreated, and cold or drying only slows it.
field_note.yearofice.raw_hide.rule: Work a hide soon after the kill, or it spoils.
field_note.yearofice.hare_pelt.fact: The snowshoe hare turns white in winter and brown in summer, driven by the length of the day.
field_note.yearofice.hare_pelt.rule: Its pelt is warm but thin; it takes several to make a garment.
field_note.yearofice.snare_wire.fact: A snare works with the animal's own movement: the harder it pulls, the tighter the loop closes.
field_note.yearofice.snare_wire.rule: Set it on a trail, check it often, and never in your own camp.
field_note.yearofice.snare_set.fact: Snowshoe hares follow the same trails every day, so a loop set on a trail takes them reliably.
field_note.yearofice.snare_set.rule: Place snares along tracks and runs, not in open ground.
field_note.yearofice.rabbit_starvation.f: Hare is lean. A diet of only very lean meat causes illness, known as rabbit starvation.
field_note.yearofice.rabbit_starvation.r: Eat the fat with the meat, or add berries and fish.
field_note.yearofice.ptarmigan.fact: The willow ptarmigan is the only grouse that turns white in winter, and it dives into snow to roost.
field_note.yearofice.ptarmigan.rule: Winter birds are harder to see, but easy to track in the snow.
field_note.yearofice.arctic_grayling.fac: Arctic grayling spawn in spring and gather in clear, cold, fast water; they are named for the sail-like dorsal fin.
field_note.yearofice.arctic_grayling.rul: Fish the clear riffles in the morning and evening.
field_note.yearofice.worm_bait.fact: Worms work as bait because grayling feed on drifting insects and anything moving like one.
field_note.yearofice.worm_bait.rule: Bait the hook and let it drift with the current.
field_note.yearofice.fishing_rod.fact: A bent rod stores energy like a spring and tires a fish without breaking the line.
field_note.yearofice.fishing_rod.rule: Keep the rod bent and give line when the fish pulls hard.
field_note.yearofice.dried_fish.fact: Drying removes the water that bacteria need, so dried fish keeps for months.
field_note.yearofice.dried_fish.rule: Dried fish and pemmican are the food you carry; fresh food is the food you eat today.
field_note.yearofice.pemmican.fact: Pemmican, dried meat pounded with rendered fat, was the travelling food of the northern fur trade and kept for a year or more.
field_note.yearofice.pemmican.rule: It packs the most calories for its weight of anything you can carry.
field_note.yearofice.moose_meat.fact: A moose can weigh over 400 kilograms; a single kill is more meat than one person can keep before it spoils.
field_note.yearofice.moose_meat.rule: A big kill means a big job: cut, dry or cache it fast.
field_note.yearofice.fat_energy.fact: Fat has more than twice the calories of protein or carbohydrate for the same weight.
field_note.yearofice.fat_energy.rule: In the cold, fat is the food that keeps you going longest.
field_note.yearofice.cooking_pot.fact: Boiling water for a minute kills the germs that make clear mountain water unsafe.
field_note.yearofice.cooking_pot.rule: Boil water from ponds and rivers before you drink it.
field_note.yearofice.kettle.fact: Cast iron holds heat well and spreads it evenly, so it cooks without scorching.
field_note.yearofice.kettle.rule: A kettle on the fire keeps water ready for tea and cooking.
field_note.yearofice.felling_axe.fact: A felling axe cuts across the grain, and a notch on the fall side steers the tree.
field_note.yearofice.felling_axe.rule: Cut the notch on the side you want the tree to fall.
field_note.yearofice.bucksaw.fact: A bucksaw cuts on the pull and the push, which makes firewood lengths much faster than an axe.
field_note.yearofice.bucksaw.rule: Saw logs to length, then split them.
field_note.yearofice.firewood_split.fact: Split wood dries faster than a round log because its inside is open to the air.
field_note.yearofice.firewood_split.rule: Split wood burns hotter and catches quicker than rounds.
field_note.yearofice.bow_drill.fact: A bow drill turns a spindle fast enough that friction makes a glowing ember in a few minutes of steady work.
field_note.yearofice.bow_drill.rule: Keep the stroke long and the downward pressure steady.
field_note.yearofice.match_strike.fact: A match head ignites at around 180 degrees Celsius, from friction against a striking surface.
field_note.yearofice.match_strike.rule: Keep matches dry: damp heads will not strike.
field_note.yearofice.tinder_flame.fact: Fire needs three things at once: heat, fuel and air; take away any one and it dies.
field_note.yearofice.tinder_flame.rule: Feed it in order: tinder, then kindling, then bigger wood.
field_note.yearofice.small_fire.fact: Most of a campfire's warmth reaches you as radiant heat, which warms the side facing the fire far more than the side turned away.
field_note.yearofice.small_fire.rule: Face the fire to warm up, and turn to dry the other side.
field_note.yearofice.fire_ring_set.fact: A ring of stones keeps coals from drifting and holds the heat in.
field_note.yearofice.fire_ring_set.rule: Build fires inside a ring, away from dry grass and from low branches.
field_note.yearofice.coals.fact: Coals glow for hours and hold more heat than flames, which is why they are the best part of a fire for cooking.
field_note.yearofice.coals.rule: Let the fire burn down to coals before cooking meat.
field_note.yearofice.bough_bed.fact: Spruce boughs trap air, and a thick layer stops the ground from drawing the heat out of your body while you sleep.
field_note.yearofice.bough_bed.rule: Sleep on boughs, not on bare ground or snow.
field_note.yearofice.spruce_boughs.fact: Boughs from living spruce regrow, and a few from each tree harm it far less than felling one.
field_note.yearofice.spruce_boughs.rule: Take a few from many trees, not all from one.
field_note.yearofice.messenger.fact: Cold drains batteries because it slows the chemical reactions inside them; a battery kept warm lasts far longer.
field_note.yearofice.messenger.rule: Keep the messenger inside your coat to save its battery.
field_note.yearofice.crate_pack.fact: Carrying about a fifth of your body weight is comfortable for hours; far more slows you and wears you out.
field_note.yearofice.crate_pack.rule: Watch the load meter: a heavy pack costs energy on every step.
field_note.yearofice.spit_set.fact: Cooking over a fire on a spit turns meat evenly, so it browns outside and cooks through.
field_note.yearofice.spit_set.rule: Turn the spit; meat on one side only burns while the middle stays raw.
credits.yearofice.title: Credits
messenger.yearofice.body.calories_low: You are behind on food: %s kcal over the day.
messenger.yearofice.body.digit_lost: You have lost a finger or toe: %s gone in all.
body.yearofice.part.head: head
messenger.yearofice.body.ill_gut_illness: Your stomach turns. Something you drank or ate was bad. Rest, boiled water and sips of broth.
messenger.yearofice.body.ill_fever_1: Fever: hot, then chills, in turns. It comes with the sick stomach.
messenger.yearofice.body.vomit: You are sick. Half of what you ate lately is gone, and water with it.
messenger.yearofice.body.ill_scurvy_1: Gums ache and old scars sting. A month without vitamin C: rose hips, berries, spruce tips, raw liver or fish.
messenger.yearofice.body.ill_scurvy_2: Weakness. Scurvy slows your healing and you burn more food. Eat vitamin C.
messenger.yearofice.body.ill_scurvy_3: Joints ache and walking is slow. Severe scurvy. Eat vitamin C today.
messenger.yearofice.body.ill_tapeworm_1: A parasite from raw fish or game. You absorb less of what you eat. Only medicine clears it.
messenger.yearofice.body.ill_trichinella: Parasites from raw bear meat. You absorb less and cannot feel fully well. Wormwood tea or medicine clears it.
messenger.yearofice.body.ill_botulism_1: Botulism from the sour fish. Nausea and weakness. Rest in a bed; only time cures it.
messenger.yearofice.body.ill_botulism_en: The poison has run its course.
messenger.yearofice.body.ill_lean_meat_1: Lean-meat sickness: all protein and no fat. Eat fat.
messenger.yearofice.body.ill_lean_meat_2: Lean-meat nausea: you absorb less. Eat fat for two days.
messenger.yearofice.body.ill_taste_sick_: That bite was toxic. You are weak for a day.
messenger.yearofice.body.ill_overuse_rem: Too much of that remedy today. You are drained until tomorrow.
messenger.yearofice.body.face_sunburn: Face sunburned. Grease it before the snow.
messenger.yearofice.body.face_windburn: Face windburned. Grease it against the wind.
messenger.yearofice.body.face_greased: Grease rubbed in. Your face is safe from glare and wind for eight hours.
messenger.yearofice.body.beard_iced: Your beard has iced up. Ten minutes at a fire.
messenger.yearofice.encounter.stay_down: Stay down. Moving now draws it back.
messenger.yearofice.warn.problem_cut: Cut on your %s (%s). It bleeds until dressed.
messenger.yearofice.warn.problem_cut_2: Deep cut on your %s (%s). It bleeds hard: bandage it.
messenger.yearofice.warn.problem_burn: Burned your %s (%s). Cool it within 10 minutes.
messenger.yearofice.warn.problem_burn_2: Bad burn on your %s (%s). It is an open wound.
messenger.yearofice.warn.problem_sprain_: Badly sprained your %s (%s). Wrap it and rest.
messenger.yearofice.warn.problem_bruise: Bruised your %s (%s). A night's rest or a bandage helps.
messenger.yearofice.warn.pack_took_it: The pack took the first hit.
messenger.yearofice.warn.back_strained: Wrenched your back. Lift with your legs.
messenger.yearofice.warn.cauterized: Cauterized your %s. Bleeding stopped; the burn is open.
messenger.yearofice.warn.cauterize_black: Cauterized, and you black out where you lie.
messenger.yearofice.body.frost_nip: Frostnip on your hands, feet or face: white and numb. Warm it up.
messenger.yearofice.body.frost_superfici: Frostbite: blisters are forming. Get out of the cold and rewarm slowly.
messenger.yearofice.body.frost_deep: Deep frostbite. The skin is black. Rewarm it now.
messenger.yearofice.body.frost_digit_los: The frostbite took a finger or toe for good.

messenger.yearofice.pickup.deadfall_slip: The rock slipped as you set it. A cut finger.
messenger.yearofice.pickup.deadfall_brok: The sticks are split. Notch new ones.
messenger.yearofice.pickup.deadfall_mous: A mouse under the stone. Marten bait.
messenger.yearofice.pickup.deadfall_take: A hare under the rock, stiff and cold.
messenger.yearofice.pickup.pan_black_san: Black grains left in the pan: iron.
